grades.quote: The `SLT` instruction performs the operation that compares the data in the general register `rj` with the data in the general register `rk` as signed integers.
grades.reason: Directly describes LoongArch SLT (signed) and SLTU (unsigned) comparison instructions and contrasts how each compares rj and rk and sets rd.

grades.quote: The value in general register `rj` and general register `rk` are compared as signed numbers. If the comparison conditions are not met, an exception for address bound checking is triggered.
grades.reason: Describes a signed-only comparison that raises an exception (bound check) rather than setting a result. It has no unsigned counterpart, so it only partly relates to the query.

grades.quote: BLT and BLTU take the branch if _rs1_ is less than _rs2_ , using signed and unsigned comparison respectively. BGE and BGEU take the branch if _rs1_ is greater than or equal to _rs2_ , using signed and unsigned comparison respectively.
grades.reason: Explains RISC-V compare-and-branch instructions in signed and unsigned forms (BLT/BLTU, BGE/BGEU), so it directly answers the signed vs unsigned comparison question.

grades.quote: Existing 64-bit wide SLTU and unsigned branch compares still operate correctly on unsigned 32-bit integers under this invariant.
grades.reason: Only mentions in passing that existing 64-bit SLTU and unsigned branch compares work on sign-extended unsigned 32-bit values. It doesn't describe the signed or unsigned comparison instructions themselves.
